findings.issue: Cross-ref imprecision: §5.3(b) does not actually show the '640 − 140 − 64' arithmetic. Page 104 (§5.3(b)) shows '640 GB total HBM − 140 GB weights = 500 GB headroom (before the ~64 GB runtime reserve that the concurrency budget in Ch 7 subtracts to reach the ~436 GB KV budget)' — it explicitly delegates the '−64' step to Ch 7. The parenthetical implies §5.3(b) is the source of the full subtraction.
findings.fix_instruction: Change '§5.3(b)' to 'Ch 7 §7.3' (or '§5.3(b) and Ch 7 §7.3'), since the −64 subtraction is derived in Ch 7.

findings.chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
findings.evidence: §5.3(a): "... ~186–371 ms if encoded on a single CPU core at ~30–60 GFLOP/s sustained (~200 GFLOP/s is the AVX-512 theoretical peak, not a sustained rate), but only ~1.1 ms on a ~10 TFLOP/s GPU, which is the basis the ~120 ms retrieval budget already assumes (vector search and reranking on a local GPU, Ch 4). On that basis the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget; single-core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s), beyond the typical sustained range (371 ms at 30 GFLOP/s vs 186 ms at 60 GFLOP/s) — conditional on measured single-core throughput."
findings.issue: The sentence "the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget" is immediately contradicted by the figures in the same sentence for the CPU case (186–371 ms > 120 ms). The referent of "On that basis" is ambiguous: it can only mean the GPU figure (~1.1 ms), yet the following clause re-argues the CPU case, so the reader cannot tell which basis the claim is made on. The claim is also the hinge for the paragraph's conclusion that "the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget".
findings.fix_instruction: Split the sentence and name the basis explicitly: "On a GPU (~1.1 ms at ~10 TFLOP/s) the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget; on a single CPU core it does not — 186–371 ms at 30–60 GFLOP/s — so single-core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core." Keep the numbers as they are; only the referents need to be disambiguated.
